youtube.title: The Army Announced It Captured a Flying Saucer. Here's What It Really Was. | Roswell
youtube.description:
In the summer of 1947, rancher Mac Brazel found strange wreckage on his land near Roswell, New Mexico. Roswell Army Air Field's intelligence officer, Major Jesse Marcel, collected it, and the base issued a statement: "The many rumors regarding the flying disc became a reality yesterday." On 8 July 1947 the Roswell Daily Record ran the headline "RAAF Captures Flying Saucer On Ranch in Roswell Region." Within a day, Gen. Roger Ramey announced it was a weather balloon. In 1994, a US Air Force report concluded the weather-balloon story was not the whole truth: the debris came from Project Mogul, a then-classified balloon project.

📂 Case File #033: Roswell 1947

Sources: History.com, "What Really Happened at Roswell"; The Debrief, "Famous Roswell UFO Incident Celebrates 75th Anniversary"; US Air Force, "Report of Air Force Research Regarding the Roswell Incident" (1994).
